![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

When performing file reads, wrap the operations in try-catch blocks to catch errors and convert them into stable, typed failure diagnostics with a nonzero fail-closed exit code or failure verdict, rather than throwing raw exceptions.

```javascript
const sample = canary.objects[0];
let bytes;
try {
  bytes = await readFile(path.resolve(root, sample.source_pdf_path));
} catch (error) {
  return {
    schema_version: RECEIPT_SCHEMA,
    target: 'local_fake_disposable_storage',
    source_document_id: sample.source_document_id,
    object_key: sample.object_key,
    expected_sha256: sample.sha256,
    write_observed_sha256: '0'.repeat(64),
    readback_sha256: '0'.repeat(64),
    byte_readback_pass: false,
    denial_probes: [],
    denial_pass: false,
    reconciliation: { expected_count: 0, actual_count: 0, orphan_keys: [], missing_keys: [] },
    rollback: planRollback([]),
    rollback_pass: false,
    counters: { local_fake_writes: 0, remote_mutations: ledger.remote },
    remote_target_contacted: false,
    credentials_loaded: false,
    verdict: 'fail',
    error: `Failed to read source PDF file: ${error.message}`
  };
}
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When performing file reads or external inspections (such as PDF parsing), wrap the operations in try-catch blocks to catch errors and convert them into stable, typed failure diagnostics with a nonzero fail-closed exit code.
</details>

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate plans on clean byte verification**

When reviewers run `node scripts/storage-spine/cli.mjs upload-dry-run` or `plan`, this path emits `object-plan.dry-run.v1.json` directly from the frozen registry without running `buildDriftSnapshot`; `planObjects` only copies the registered paths/bytes/hashes and never stats or hashes the source PDFs. If a local source PDF is missing or has drifted, the command still produces a full `would_upload` plan and zero-remote evidence, even though the ADR says local byte size and SHA-256 are verified before producing a plan.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve full evidence hashes for subcommands**

In the documented reproduce sequence, running `upload-dry-run` after `npm run storage-spine:stg-01` leaves the checked-in evidence dirty because `results` contains only `plan`, so this recomputes `artifacts_sha256` with just the plan hash and overwrites the previous snapshot/canary/rehearsal hashes. I verified that exact sequence changes `zero-remote-mutation-evidence.v1.json`; either avoid rewriting the aggregate evidence for partial commands or merge/read the existing artifact hashes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject bytes that do not match the content key**

When the local fake storage is used to rehearse create-only content-addressed writes, `put` accepts any bytes for any syntactically valid `sha256/.../<digest>.pdf` key and only reports the observed hash after the write. That lets a rehearsal store bytes under a digest they do not match, undermining the immutable object identity/collision checks this fake is supposed to model; parse the digest from the key and fail before writing when `sha256(bytes)` differs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the frozen origin/main baseline**

The contract freezes both the registry hash and `baseline.origin_main_sha`, but `loadFrozenRegistry` only validates the registry bytes and never checks that `origin/main` still resolves to the frozen SHA. In a checkout where `origin/main` has advanced, the CLI will still emit a passing snapshot/evidence package that cites the old baseline, so the provenance lock can silently go stale unless this function verifies the ref or stops claiming it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require each denial role exactly once**

The receipt schema caps `denial_probes` at three entries, but each entry only has to be one of the allowed roles, so a receipt with three `anon` denials and no `authenticated` or `browser` probe still validates. Since this contract is the evidence that all three non-authority roles were denied, add per-role `contains`/`minContains` checks or an equivalent uniqueness rule.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
